topic: Field expertise — UAE codes, standards & specs
content:
Tents & Shade Structures in the UAE operate under a layered approval framework that varies by emirate, location type, and intended use. In Dubai, any temporary or semi-permanent tent or shade structure erected for public gatherings, events, or commercial use requires a No Objection Certificate from Dubai Civil Defence (DCD), which evaluates fire safety compliance against the UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice — covering flame-retardancy of fabric, emergency exit widths, fire extinguisher placement, and maximum occupancy loads. Dubai Municipality issues structural permits for ground-anchored installations and reviews wind-load calculations; for structures on private plots or within master-planned communities, the Dubai Development Authority (DDA) or the relevant master developer may hold concurrent jurisdiction. Structures within port zones, Jebel Ali Free Zone, or Trakhees-regulated areas must obtain Trakhees NOC separately. For Abu Dhabi, the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) and Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority (ADCD) hold equivalent roles.

Relevant technical standards include EN 13782 (temporary structures — tents) for structural design and safety, NFPA 102 for grandstands, folding and telescopic seating, tents, and membrane structures, and CPAI-84 for fabric flame resistance. Wind-load design must reference UAE climatic data; Dubai sits in a high-wind-dust zone and structures are typically engineered for sustained winds of 120–160 km/h minimum. Fabric specifications centre on PVC-coated polyester (typically 650–900 gsm for event tents), HDPE knitted shade cloth (rated by shade factor percentage, commonly 90–95% for car parks and walkways), and PTFE or ETFE tensile membrane for premium permanent canopies. Key structural elements include aluminium or galvanised-steel frame systems, tensioned cable networks, ground anchors or ballast blocks (critical where ground penetration is restricted), ridge poles, purlins, and anti-ponding drainage slopes. Electrical fit-out inside tents requires DEWA-compliant temporary power connections and DCD sign-off on internal wiring.

Price drivers include fabric grade and UV-stabilisation rating, structure span and clear height, anchor method (ballast vs. ground screw vs. concrete footing), fire-rated lining requirements, air-conditioning integration (evaporative coolers vs. ducted split systems), custom branding or printing, and mobilisation distance. Rental versus purchase models diverge sharply on cost.

Compliance pitfalls include using non-flame-retardant fabric that fails DCD inspection, inadequate wind-load engineering stamps from a UAE-licensed civil engineer, missing occupancy calculations for public events, and overlooking Trakhees jurisdiction in free-zone venues. Sharp qualifying questions: What is the intended use — event, permanent shade, car park, or construction hoarding? Is the site Dubai Municipality, Trakhees, or master-developer jurisdiction? Is a DCD event permit already initiated? What is the expected occupancy and duration? Is electrical power or AC required inside? Are ground anchors permitted or is ballast-only

topic: What drives price in UAE tents & shades
content: The biggest cost drivers are: (1) Temporary rental vs permanent supply-and-install — rental (event tents, Ramadan tents, majlis) is priced per day/week and includes setup and dismantle, while permanent shades (car park, warehouse, walkway) are a one-time CAPEX with engineering and fixings. (2) Span and clear height — free-span structures over 15-20m need heavier aluminium box-truss and cost far more than pole/frame tents. (3) Fabric grade — standard PVC (single/double-coated), PVDF-lacquered PVC for UV/dust longevity, HDPE knitted mesh for shade sails, or Tensile PTFE/ETFE membranes for architectural work. (4) Wind loading — UAE structures are commonly designed for 100-150 km/h gusts; higher ratings mean more steel/foundations. (5) Foundations — bolted to existing slab is cheap; new concrete footings, kerbs or ground anchors add cost. (6) Accessories — flooring/decking, AC ducting, sidewalls, lighting, glass walls, gutters. (7) Site conditions — sand vs concrete, access, remoteness (Al Dhafra/Liwa jobs carry mobilisation), and whether crane access is needed. (8) Quantity and repetition lower per-unit cost. Summer heat also drives demand for AC-integrated tents and thermal-insulated fabrics.

topic: Specs a customer MUST provide for a firm quote
content: To price without a site visit, suppliers need: purpose (event, majlis, car park, walkway, warehouse, storage, labour accommodation shade, poolside); rental or permanent supply; required dimensions — length x width in metres and clear height (or number of parking bays for car park shades); the emirate and specific area; mounting surface (existing concrete slab, asphalt, interlock, sand/ground); duration if rental (days/weeks/months) with exact dates; fabric preference or 'recommend' (standard PVC / PVDF / HDPE mesh / tensile membrane); wind-rating expectation (standard event vs engineered permanent); accessories needed (AC, flooring, sidewalls, lighting, glass front, gutters); and any authority/permit requirement. For permanent structures, a photo of the site and a rough layout/marked plan hugely improves accuracy. For events, confirm number of guests or seating layout so span can be sized. Stating whether you already have a drawing/DEWA-type approval or need the supplier to handle it avoids re-quoting. Clarify if a colour/branding requirement exists — printed fabric and custom colours add lead time and cost.

Temporary event tents in Dubai typically require a permit from Dubai Municipality (Building Permits) and often Dubai Civil Defence (DCD) approval for fire-retardant fabric and emergency egress, especially for public/large events; event venues may also need DTCM/Dubai Economy event approvals. Fabrics for public tents should carry fire-retardant certification (commonly to NFPA 701 or EN 13501/B-s1,d0 equivalents) — suppliers should provide the certificate. In Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi City Municipality and Abu Dhabi Civil Defence (via the ADCD/QCC framework) govern permits and fire safety. Permanent structures (car park shades, tensile canopies) are treated as building works: they need structural design by a licensed UAE engineer, municipality building permit, and in some communities approval from the master developer (e.g., Nakheel, Emaar, Aldar) or free zone authority. Car park shades on public/community areas often follow developer specs. Wind design generally references relevant loading standards and Emirates-specific requirements; foundations may need soil consideration on sand. Always confirm who obtains permits — you or the supplier — as this affects scope, timeline and cost.

Frequent gaps: (1) Not stating mounting surface — a shade priced for bolting to a slab is very different from one needing new footings in sand. (2) Forgetting AC in summer — an uncooled tent is unusable May-September, and retrofit AC/ducting costs more. (3) Ignoring permits and fire certification, then getting shut down by Civil Defence on event day. (4) Under-sizing height — vehicles, forklifts or catering need clear headroom; car park shades must clear SUVs and roof boxes. (5) Assuming rental price includes flooring, sidewalls, lighting and cleaning — these are usually add-ons. (6) Not accounting for dismantle/removal at end of rental. (7) Overlooking master-developer/community approval for permanent structures in gated communities. (8) Providing no dates for rentals — peak Ramadan, National Day and Q1 event season have limited stock and premium pricing. (9) Forgetting drainage/gutters for the winter rain months. (10) Not specifying whether the shade must be relocatable vs permanently fixed.

Rental (event/majlis) usually INCLUDES: structure frame and fabric, transport, installation and dismantle, basic anchoring/ballast. Usually EXCLUDES: AC, flooring/carpet/decking, lighting and power, furniture, sidewalls/glass, branding print, permits and Civil Defence fees, security, and standby technicians unless specified. Permanent supply-and-install usually INCLUDES: structural steel/aluminium, fabric, standard powder-coated finish, bolting to existing slab, and manufacturer warranty on fabric (commonly a stated number of years for PVDF/HDPE). Usually EXCLUDES: concrete footings/civil works, drawings and structural stamping, municipality/developer permit fees, electrical/lighting integration, drainage connection, and painting to non-standard RAL colours. For both, confirm whether making-good of the surface, crane/access equipment, and disposal are included. Warranty terms vary by fabric: HDPE shade mesh and PVDF membranes carry longer UV warranties than standard PVC. Always ask what the anchoring method is and whether it suits your surface.

Run through: (1) Rental or permanent supply? (2) Application — event/majlis, car park, walkway, warehouse/storage, industrial? (3) Dimensions: L x W x clear height, or number of car bays. (4) Emirate and specific location, plus site access/remoteness. (5) Mounting surface: existing slab, asphalt, interlock, or sand. (6) Fabric: standard PVC, PVDF, HDPE mesh, tensile membrane — or recommend. (7) Wind rating: standard event vs engineered permanent. (8) Duration and exact dates if rental. (9) Accessories: AC, flooring, sidewalls, lighting, glass, gutters, branding. (10) Foundations/civil works needed? (11) Permits and fire certification — who handles? (12) Community/developer or free-zone approval required? (13) Quantity/repetition. (14) Crane or special access. (15) Warranty expectation. With these, produce a fixed price separating supply, install, and excluded civil/permit items; flag assumptions clearly (e.g., 'priced assuming bolt-down to existing concrete slab').
Ask: Tiles / marble / granite? [MANDATORY]; Area (sq ft)? [MANDATORY]; Floor / wall / both?; Wet area?; Material supplied by you or the supplier?; Pattern/finish?; Timeline? Never ask budget.

1) Material: natural marble, granite, limestone, travertine, onyx, engineered/quartz stone, or porcelain tile? 2) Application: floor, wall cladding, stairs/risers, countertop/vanity, skirting, feature wall, external? 3) Area in m2 and linear metres (skirting/edges/stairs), plus piece sizes? 4) Property/space type: villa, apartment, hotel/lobby, retail, bathroom, kitchen? 5) Stone origin/grade preference (Italian, Turkish, Spanish, Indian granite) and any specific name/colour? 6) Format and thickness: slab vs tile, required thickness (mm) for floor vs counter? 7) Finish: polished, honed, leathered, flamed (granite), brushed; and edge profile (bullnose, bevel, mitred)? 8) Slip/wet-area needs (bathroom, pool, stairs) and any slip rating? 9) Sealing/impregnation required (marble/limestone stain and etch protection)? 10) Substrate condition: bare slab, screed, old finish - removal/levelling needed? 11) Pattern/layout, book-matching, vein direction, grout colour? 12) Compliance/approvals (DM/DDA fit-out) and any heritage/landlord rules? 13) Supply & install or supply-only; who supplies stone; site access for heavy slabs? 14) Timeline, working-hours limits, budget range, and VAT shown separately?

A complete tiling & marble quote shows, per item: stone/material type and origin (e.g. Italian Carrara, Persian, Spanish; granite colour), format (slab vs tile) and size, thickness (mm), finish (polished/honed/leather/flamed), edge profile, substrate prep (screed/self-levelling, slurry bond coat), fixing method (cement mortar/adhesive class or epoxy), grouting/pointing, sealing/impregnation, skirting/risers/nosing, polishing/crystallisation, cutting/fabrication, and supply & install vs supply-only. Differentiating spec parameters (with units): stone origin/grade, thickness (e.g. 18/20mm slabs, 20mm counters, 30mm floors), finish type, water absorption/porosity, and for ceramic/porcelain the PEI and slip R-rating. A strong quote names origin, thickness, finish, adhesive/mortar class (EN 12004 C2 for stone) and includes sealing and polishing; an underpriced one cuts corners with thinner stone (e.g. 15-16mm where 18-20mm specified), lower-grade/B-grade or filled stone, cheaper cement mortar instead of proper C2 adhesive or stone-safe (non-staining white) adhesive, no penetrating sealer (marble stains/etches), reduced/skipped levelling, and skipped final polish/crystallisation. Highlight to customers: stone origin and thickness, finish, sealing inclusion, adhesive/mortar suitability for stone, and edge/skirting work. Common tricks: supply-only quoted like installed, sealing/polishing excluded, skirting and special cuts excluded, VAT and wastage hidden, off-origin substitution ('Italian look'), and vague 'marble work' with no thickness, origin or finish.

topic: Field expertise — UAE codes, standards & specs
content:
Tiling & Marble Work in the UAE operates under Dubai Municipality (DM) as the primary regulatory body for construction quality and building compliance. All tiling and marble installations in new builds or major fit-outs must align with the Dubai Building Code (DBC), which consolidates structural, material, and finishing requirements. For projects within free zones and port areas, Trakhees (PCFC Engineering) holds jurisdiction and issues its own fit-out permits and NOCs. The Dubai Development Authority (DDA) governs projects in designated development zones such as Dubai Design District and similar areas. No dedicated DCD or SIRA approvals apply to tiling work itself, though if tiling interfaces with fire-rated walls or floors, the installer must not compromise fire-compartmentation ratings — DCD sign-off on the broader fit-out may be required. For commercial fit-outs, a Fit-Out Permit from the relevant authority (DM, Trakhees, or DDA) is mandatory before work commences, and a completion inspection is required before handover.

Applicable standards include ASTM C627 (Robinson Floor Test for tile installation systems), ASTM C650 (chemical resistance), ASTM C1028 / BS 7976 (slip resistance), EN 14411 (ceramic tile classification), ISO 10545 series (dimensional tolerances, water absorption, breaking strength), and BS 5385 (wall and floor tiling practice). UAE's ESMA enforces conformity marks on imported tile products; CE or ESMA conformity documentation is frequently demanded by DM inspectors.

Core scope covers rectified vs. non-rectified porcelain, natural stone (Carrara, Nero Marquina, Crema Marfil, local UAE beige marble), engineered stone, large-format slabs (1200×2400mm and beyond), book-matching, waterjet cutting, CNC profiling, epoxy vs. cementitious grout, flexible adhesive (C2TE classification per EN 12004), movement joints, waterproofing membranes beneath wet-area tiles, and substrate preparation (screeds, self-levelling compounds). Marble polishing grades (honed, polished, brushed, leathered), edge profiles (bullnose, ogee, bevelled), and skirting integration are standard discussion points. Anti-fracture membranes, heated-floor compatibility, and large-format lippage control (laser-guided levelling clips) are increasingly specified.

Price drivers include stone origin and rarity, slab thickness (18mm vs. 20mm vs. 30mm), wastage factor (pattern complexity, book-matching), surface area vs. linear cutting ratio, subfloor condition and levelling depth, access difficulty (high-rise, occupied premises), and grout/adhesive specification tier.

Compliance pitfalls include using non-ESMA-conformant tiles on DM-inspected projects, inadequate waterproofing in bathrooms leading to structural moisture claims, ignoring movement joint requirements causing cracking, and specifying adhesive not rated for large-format tiles. The agent should ask: What is the project type and authority jurisdiction

Tiling and marble work is delivered within fit-out or construction and needs the relevant permit by location: Dubai Municipality (DM) Building Permit System for mainland, Dubai Development Authority (DDA) fit-out permit in its free-zone districts, or Trakhees for Nakheel/free-zone areas; the contractor must be DM/DDA-licensed and drawings submitted by a licensed consultant. The Dubai Building Code and DM finishing guidelines apply, including slip resistance in wet and public areas. Dubai Civil Defence (DCD) NOC is relevant where stone/tiling affects fire compartmentation, escape routes or cladding fire performance; obtain NOCs as required. Stone, tiles, adhesives and sealers are subject to ESMA/MoIAT conformity (ECAS) and should carry test/quality documentation; imported natural stone may also need standard customs/quality documentation. For major fit-outs affecting 50%+ of built-up area, Al Sa'fat 2.0 Silver sustainability compliance can apply, which can affect material sourcing and low-VOC sealers/adhesives. Practical workflow: appoint licensed contractor/consultant, prepare finishes/setting-out drawings, obtain any DCD NOC, secure fit-out/building permit (DM/DDA/Trakhees), install to spec with proper sealing, then inspection and completion sign-off. Always confirm the governing authority by the project's exact location before committing to a programme.

Natural stone: marble (calcareous, polishable, prone to staining/etching - needs sealing), granite (hard, durable, suitable for counters/heavy floors), limestone/travertine (porous, sealing critical), onyx (decorative). Typical thicknesses: slabs 18-20mm, countertops 20mm, floor slabs up to 30mm, wall tiles thinner. Finishes: polished (reflective), honed (matt, less slip), leathered/brushed, flamed (granite, slip-resistant external). Quality vocabulary: origin/grade, porosity/water absorption, flexural strength, and whether stone is filled/resin-treated. Fixing: cement mortar/slurry for thick beds, or notched-trowel adhesive to EN 12004 (C2 improved, often a non-staining white or stone-specific adhesive to avoid discolouration), grouts to EN 13888; large/heavy slabs may need anchored/mechanical fixing on facades. Sealing uses penetrating impregnators; marble is finished by polishing and crystallisation. For ceramic/porcelain tiling, the same PEI (abrasion 1-5), DIN 51130 R-rating (slip) and water-absorption metrics apply. Reputable supply: Italian/Spanish/Turkish marble houses and UAE stone suppliers; adhesives/sealers by Mapei, Sika, Weber, Laticrete, Sodamco. Match stone thickness to application, use stone-safe adhesive, and always specify sealing for marble/limestone.

Indicative UAE prices (verify per project; exclude VAT 5% unless stated). Material supply varies hugely by stone: granite slabs roughly AED 250-650/m2 (entry to premium), polished marble at 20mm roughly from ~AED 185/m2 for common types up to several hundred or thousands for premium Italian/exotic; porcelain marble-effect tiles are cheaper. Marble/stone installation labour commonly roughly AED 35-80/m2 depending on complexity, with stairs, mitred edges, book-matching and large slabs adding cost; sealing, polishing and crystallisation are separate. Price drivers: stone origin/grade, thickness, finish, piece size/slab handling, edge and skirting work, substrate levelling, sealing/polishing, and access for heavy slabs. Red flags: prices far below market usually mean thinner stone (15-16mm vs 18-20mm), lower-grade/filled/B-grade stone or origin substitution, cement mortar or a staining grey adhesive instead of stone-safe C2 adhesive, no penetrating sealer (leading to staining/etching), skipped levelling, and no final polish/crystallisation. Also watch for supply-only disguised as installed, excluded sealing/polishing, excluded skirting/stairs/special cuts, hidden VAT and wastage, and vague 'marble work' with no stated origin, thickness or finish. Confirm a sealing line item exists for marble/limestone.

Ask: Which area (roof / bathroom / basement / water tank / balcony / podium)? [MANDATORY]; Approx area (sq ft)? [MANDATORY]; New application or leak repair?; System preference or advise?; Access? Note: Municipality wet-area waterproofing standards. Never ask budget.

1. Which substrates/zones need waterproofing - roof, podium deck, basement raft/retaining wall, bathroom/wet area, kitchen/laundry, water tank (potable?), pool, planter/landscape, balcony/terrace? Each has a different correct system. 2. New construction, refurbishment, or active-leak remediation (remediation needs leak diagnosis first)? 3. Total area per zone (m2) and number of penetrations (drains, pipes, anchors)? 4. Is this in a developer-managed community (Emaar, Nakheel), a free zone (DDA/Trakhees/TECOM) or standard DM jurisdiction? Determines whose NOC/fit-out approval and material spec applies. 5. Is a DM fit-out permit or developer NOC required (any wet-area relocation/MEP change typically triggers it)? 6. Is DCL-certified material mandated by the consultant/developer, and a specific approved brand/system? 7. What warranty is required - is 10-year full-system coverage specified? 8. Exposed or covered system (exposed roof PU needs a UV-stable aliphatic topcoat; buried needs protection screed/board)? 9. Substrate condition: existing cracks, dampness, prior failed membrane to remove, structural movement, negative-side water pressure? 10. Groundwater/high water table for basement tanking (Dubai coastal areas have aggressive saline groundwater), and is there a soil/groundwater report? 11. Required service life and budget tier (economy bitumen vs premium PU/sheet)? 12. Access and scheduling: occupied building, work at height, confined space (tanks/lift pits), traffic over podium needing a trafficable system? 13. Will a flood/ponding test be permitted and witnessed, and who signs off? 14. Will the contractor provide system data sheets, MSDS, DCL/conformity certificate and a method statement for approval before starting?

A compliant Dubai waterproofing quote is line-itemed by substrate/zone, exposing the full system rather than 'supply and apply membrane'. Demand: measured area m2 per zone (not lump-sum) - roof, podium, basement raft, retaining wall, each bathroom/wet area, water tank, planter, pool; system type named explicitly (liquid-applied PU/acrylic, cementitious 1- or 2-component, bituminous torch-on APP or SBS, self-adhesive bitumen, PVC/TPO/HDPE/EPDM sheet, or crystalline); number of coats (liquid) or plies (sheet) - PU/cementitious wet areas typically 2-3 coats, torch-on roofs typically 2 layers; DFT in microns/mm for liquid and membrane thickness mm for sheet (commonly 3-4 mm torch-on, 1.2-2.0 mm PVC/TPO, 1.5-2.0 mm HDPE); the manufacturer's matched primer (bitumen primer for torch-on, epoxy/PU for liquid on concrete); reinforcement mesh/fleece at coves, joints, drains and pipe penetrations; mortar fillet/coving at wall-floor junctions; surface prep (grinding/shot-blasting, crack repair, laitance removal, moisture check, fall-to-drain); protection layer (screed, board, geotextile or drainage board for buried/podium/planter); flood/ponding test 24-48h with documented results; warranty (years, and material-only vs full system/applicator); GRP lining where specified; drainage detail. Compare apples-to-apples by normalising to AED/m2 by zone AND to total dry build-up (coats x DFT, or membrane mm + protection); the cheaper-per-m2 number is meaningless without the build-up. Corner cuts (almost always in invisible layers the client cannot see after completion): fewer coats/plies; lower DFT/thinner membrane; skipped primer (adhesion failure); skipped protection screed/board (membrane punctured at backfill); skipped flood test; no mesh/fillet at coves and penetrations; a cheaper non-DCL membrane substituted as 'equivalent'; no surface-prep line; lump-sum hiding a quantity shortfall; and a 'material-only' warranty disguised as a 10-year warranty.

topic: Field expertise — UAE codes, standards & specs
content:
Waterproofing Services in the UAE operates under a layered regulatory and technical environment shaped by the region's extreme heat, high humidity in coastal zones, and aggressive alkaline soils.

**Governing Authority & Approvals.** Dubai Municipality (DM) is the primary authority; its Building Regulations and Construction Specifications mandate waterproofing systems as part of structural permit compliance for new builds and major refurbishments. For projects within free zones and port areas (Jebel Ali, DP World zones), Trakhees issues the relevant construction permits and inspects waterproofing as part of structural sign-off. Projects on Dubai Development Authority (DDA) land — DIFC, Design District — require DDA building permit compliance. Abu Dhabi projects fall under Abu Dhabi City Municipality and ADDED. No standalone waterproofing NOC exists; approvals are embedded within the overall building permit and completion certificate process. Dubai Civil Defence approval is required where waterproofing intersects with fire-rated assemblies (e.g., below-grade plant rooms, fire-rated deck coatings). Contractors must hold a valid DM-registered trade licence in the "Waterproofing Works" or "Specialist Contracting" category.

**Standards.** Applicable standards include ASTM D412 (tensile properties of membranes), ASTM D4541 (pull-off adhesion), ASTM D5957 (flood testing of horizontal membranes), BS 8102 (protection of below-ground structures), BS 8217 (reinforced bitumen membranes), EN 13967 (flexible sheets for roofs), ASTM C836 (high-solids content cold liquid-applied elastomeric waterproofing), and ISO 9001 for contractor quality management. Dubai Municipality's own Construction Specifications reference British Standards and ASTM in parallel. For green-roof or podium-deck assemblies, root-resistance certification per EN 13948 is relevant.

**Scope & Specs.** Core application areas: below-grade structures (basements, lift pits, raft foundations), roofs (flat, podium, terrace), wet areas (bathrooms, kitchens, plant rooms), swimming pools, water tanks (potable-water-safe membranes required — NSF/ANSI 61 compliance), tunnels, and façade/balcony junctions. Key systems and materials discussed: torch-applied SBS/APP modified bitumen membranes (typically 3–4 mm thickness, single or double layer); cold-applied liquid membranes (polyurethane, PMMA, acrylic); cementitious crystalline systems (Xypex, Penetron-type) for concrete structures; bentonite panels for below-grade; injection grouting (polyurethane or epoxy) for remedial crack sealing; sheet membranes (HDPE, PVC, TPO) for below-slab tanking. Critical specs buyers discuss: membrane thickness (DFT — dry film thickness), elongation-at-break (≥300% for flexible membranes), hydrostatic head resistance

The Dubai Building Code (2021 Edition, official, on dm.gov.ae) is the governing technical document; its verified principle is that a full waterproof tanking system must be provided for all elements exposed to water, and structural elements that cannot be accessed for maintenance are treated specially. Exact clause numbers for wet-area/roof/basement DFTs should be confirmed in the PDF before being quoted as fact. Administrative Resolution No. (37) of 2021 (Dubai Legislation portal) amends the Bylaw on Building Requirements and Specifications and is the legal instrument behind the tanking/waterproofing requirements. Dubai Central Laboratory (DCL) product certification (verified): DCL certifies building materials against DM regulations and adopted standards, is accredited to ISO/IEC 17065 and approved by EIAC (Cert. No. CB-PRD-001), and for products not covered by an adopted standard issues a Technical Approval; the process runs initial factory assessment, product testing, certification licence, then surveillance. Identified building products - including waterproofing membranes - must carry a valid DCL Certificate of Conformity / Conformity Mark before use or sale in Dubai, and consultants routinely demand it. Approved applicator/contractor: there is no single public DM 'approved waterproofing applicator' registry found; applicator approval in practice flows through DM/Trakhees/DDA contractor licensing plus the membrane manufacturer's approved-applicator scheme tied to the system warranty (confirm with DM directly). Warranty norms: a 10-year full-system warranty is the de-facto developer-project standard (e.g. Sika systems commonly mandated on Emaar projects); note this is distinct from the Emaar homeowner Defect Liability Period of 1 year (which covers the building envelope preventing water penetration) and from the UAE Civil Code 10-year decennial liability for structural collapse. Fit-out/NOC: any wet-area relocation, partition or MEP change in DM-jurisdiction towers requires a DM fit-out permit; in free zones it routes through DDA/Trakhees fit-out permits and the developer NOC, with wet-zone changes in the strict-control category.

Standards cited for UAE waterproofing (confirm specific citations against the Code PDF before customer-facing use): EN 13707 (reinforced bituminous roof sheets); ASTM D6134 (self-adhered bituminous membranes); ASTM C836 (cold liquid-applied elastomeric PU/bituminous); plus ASTM D412/D751 (tensile/elongation), ASTM D5957 (ponding/flood test guide), ASTM E1643/E1745 (under-slab vapour barriers), ASTM D6878 (TPO), ASTM D4434 (PVC), BS 8102 (below-ground tanking reference), BS 8204 (screeds), EN 1504 (concrete repair), DIN 18195/18533 (building waterproofing). System selection by substrate: bathroom/wet area - 2-3 coats flexible cementitious or PU with mesh at coves and penetrations, mortar fillet, then 24-48h flood test before tiling; flat roof/terrace (exposed) - UV-resistant 4 mm APP torch-on (often 2 layers) or 2-component PU with aliphatic UV topcoat, laid to fall; podium/trafficable deck - heavy-duty PU or torch-on plus protection screed and drainage board; basement raft/retaining wall - full tanking per BS 8102 (pre-applied HDPE/bituminous sheet, post-applied bituminous/PU, or crystalline) with protection and drainage board, designed for negative-side hydrostatic and saline groundwater; potable water tank - 2-component flexible cementitious certified for potable contact and/or GRP, with flood test; swimming pool - 2-component cementitious or PVC sheet liner; planter - root-resistant membrane plus drainage board; lift pits/no-future-access structures - crystalline (self-healing). Materials/brands (verify each SKU's current DCL certificate): Sika (frequently mandated on Emaar - Sikalastic PU, Sikaplan PVC, SikaProof), MBCC/Master Builders Solutions MasterSeal, Fosroc (Proofex, Nitoproof), Mapei (Mapelastic), Drizoro (Maxseal/Maxelastic), and DCL-certified local makers. Indicative service life: bituminous with protection 10-15 yr; exposed PU 5-10 yr; cementitious 3-7 yr; protected PVC/TPO/HDPE sheet 15-25 yr.

Indicative AED/m2 (supply plus apply, labour included; trade-sourced ranges that vary with prep, access, thickness and warranty): overall UAE ~AED 40-175/m2; cementitious ~AED 40-70/m2; torch-on bitumen ~AED 45-75/m2; roof (system-dependent) ~AED 45-150/m2; basement from ~AED 80/m2 (basic) up to AED 500+/m2 for full structural tanking/remediation; material-only membrane rolls (1 m x 10 m, 4 mm) ~AED 130-246/roll. Where corners get cut and the red flags: fewer coats/plies than spec (the single most common cut - 1 coat instead of 2-3 leaves pinholes in corners and behind pipes); lower DFT or thinner membrane (0.8-1.0 mm where 1.5-2.0 mm is needed, or 3 mm torch-on where 4 mm is specified) - demand DFT in microns/mm; skipping the matched primer (adhesion failure from day one); skipping the protection screed/board on buried/podium/planter work (membrane punctured at backfill); skipping the flood/ponding test and its documentation (the verification step before tiling/covering); no mesh reinforcement or mortar fillet at coves and penetrations; a cheaper non-DCL membrane substituted as 'equivalent' with no Certificate of Conformity offered; no surface-prep line (prep is 30-40% of a good job); lump-sum instead of measured m2 by zone (hides quantity shortfall); and a material-only warranty disguised as a 10-year warranty (confirm it covers applicator workmanship). The corner-cutting quote is meaningfully cheaper per m2 AND silent on at least one of coat count, DFT/thickness, primer, mesh/fillet, protection layer, flood test, DCL certificate, or warranty scope.

UAE VAT (Federal Decree-Law 8/2017, amended by 16/2025 effective 1 Jan 2026) governs QuotesDone's fees. Register once taxable supplies cross the mandatory threshold (verify current AED figure with the FTA); issue valid tax invoices with TRN, correct place/time of supply and tax amount; determine place of supply for reveal fees/commissions, since services to overseas buyers/suppliers may be zero-rated exports or reverse-charged. 2026 change: self-invoicing under reverse-charge removed, so retain supplier invoices/contracts as documentation. A strict 5-year limit applies to refund claims. Reconcile VAT return boxes to the GL monthly; verify with a tax agent.

Run tight collections/treasury. Supplier dues (non-response recovery charges and circumvention sums — there is no commission on won work) are receivables: keep an aging report, chase overdue balances, hold an IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss allowance with documented write-off governance. Buyer reveal fees are collected at unlock via Stripe, never invoiced later. Use UAE instant rails (Aani) and reconcile gateway settlement to the GL daily. Enforce anti-fraud controls: dual authorisation on payments, mandatory call-back on any bank-detail change, periodic mandate review. At 50+ headcount budget Wages Protection System timing and monitor cash runway weekly.

Apply the IFRS 15 five-step model to buyer reveal fees (3% of accepted quote value; suppliers pay no commission on won work): identify contract, performance obligation (granting the buyer the chosen supplier's identity/contact), transaction price, allocation, timing. A reveal/unlock fee is normally point-in-time, satisfied when the buyer reveals the supplier - recognise it then, not when the quote is posted. Assess principal-vs-agent: if QuotesDone only connects parties and never controls the underlying goods/service, it is an agent and books the fee net, not the supplier's contract value. Capitalise only incremental costs of obtaining a contract. Track refunds/credit notes and period-end cut-off; verify treatment with the auditor.

UAE Corporate Tax (Federal Decree-Law 47/2022): 0% up to AED 375,000 taxable income and 9% above. IFRS accounting profit is the starting point, so maintain a documented tax bridge (accounting profit +/- disallowables, exempt income, timing differences, reliefs). Small Business Relief may apply to residents with revenue <= AED 3m but is time-limited (periods ending 31 Dec 2026) - confirm before year-end planning. A free-zone entity's 0% Qualifying Free Zone Person rate depends on Qualifying Income and requires audited financials. File the CT return within 9 months of year-end; keep a tax calendar. Verify rates/thresholds/free-zone conditions with the auditor.

UAE AML/CFT (Federal Decree-Law 10/2025, Cabinet Resolution 134/2025). Even as a marketplace, treat AML as an onboarding/payments concern: run KYC/CDD on suppliers and higher-risk buyers (identity, beneficial ownership, source of funds), screen against sanctions/adverse media, monitor for structuring or unusual flows. The 2025 law adds an objective 'should reasonably have known' test, regulates virtual assets/VASPs, and creates personal criminal liability for managers. If in scope, appoint an MLRO and file STRs/SARs via goAML promptly. Verify whether QuotesDone is in scope with a compliance advisor.

Build marketplace FP&A around unit economics: revenue per paid reveal (3% reveal fee; no commission on won work), effective take rate, contribution margin after processing and acquisition cost, buyer/supplier CAC, activation and repeat rates, cash runway. Model post-tax ('tax-aware FP&A') since 9% CT and VAT timing sit inside every budget/forecast/appraisal (NPV/IRR). Track paying-buyers-to-posted-quotes ratio and cohort payback. At the 50-employee threshold budget Nafis/Emiratisation fines as a contingency. Reforecast monthly against actuals with documented variance analysis; verify current tax and Nafis figures.

Keep QuotesDone audit-ready. Audited financials are mandatory for taxable persons with revenue over AED 50m and for all Qualifying Free Zone Persons regardless of revenue (verify thresholds and governing Ministerial Decision). Build the control base early: a monthly close calendar, subledger reconciliations, documented revenue cut-off, a related-party register, a COSO-style risk-control matrix mapping key assertions (revenue, cash, receivables) to controls and owners. Maintain IT general controls over billing data (access, change management, SoD). Retain contracts, invoices, gateway reports and approvals with preparer/reviewer sign-off, so the audit file is built continuously.

Choose the framework deliberately: full IFRS required once revenue exceeds AED 50m, IFRS for SMEs permitted at or below AED 50m, cash-basis allowed only for very small businesses with revenue <= AED 3m (Ministerial Decision 114/2023 - verify). Because CT taxable income starts from IFRS accounting profit, the basis drives the tax result. Maintain an accounting policy register (revenue, IFRS 16 leases, financial instruments, provisions, tax) and a disciplined month-end close: lock the GL calendar, reconcile subledgers, document manual journals, tie every disclosure to evidence. Confirm framework choice and thresholds with the auditor.

The arm's-length principle applies to ALL transactions with related parties/connected persons (owners, directors, group entities), regardless of size. Any management fees, founder loans or intercompany recharges must be priced/documented as if between independent parties. A formal Master File + Local File is required only at large scale (revenue >= AED 200m, or MNE group >= AED 3.15bn per Ministerial Decision 97/2023), but keep signed agreements, service/benefit evidence and a related-party register year-round to support the CT return. Disclose related parties in the financials. Verify thresholds with a tax agent.

ESR: Cabinet Decision 98/2024 cancelled ESR filing for financial years starting on/after 1 Jan 2023 (Corporate Tax now manages substance), though historical ESR still applies to 2019-2022 for legacy entities. Pillar Two / Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (15% minimum effective rate) applies only to large multinational groups above the EUR 750m consolidated-revenue threshold - not relevant to QuotesDone until part of such a group. Log both as monitored-not-active and re-verify if ownership/scale changes materially. Confirm current position with the auditor.

Keep Sharia-finance awareness even if QuotesDone is conventional. UAE Islamic financial institutions apply AAOIFI standards alongside IFRS, and Sharia-sensitive suppliers/buyers may prefer riba-free arrangements. If the platform ever adds financing, deferred-payment or profit-share features, structure them Sharia-compliantly (e.g. Murabaha or Wakala) and get sign-off from a qualified Sharia adviser rather than assuming a conventional interest/late-fee model is acceptable to that segment. Treat as awareness and product opportunity, not a current obligation; verify structures with a Sharia adviser before launching any Islamic product.

Operate at the level of a CFA charterholder + CPA/CMA. Command: three-statement modelling (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) and how they interlink; IFRS (and IFRS for SMEs) revenue recognition (IFRS 15) and lease/expense treatment; the 13-week cash-flow forecast for liquidity; scenario and sensitivity analysis; and capital allocation. For a marketplace: take rate, contribution margin, CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, payback period, gross vs net revenue, cohort retention, burn multiple, Rule of 40. Always separate recognised revenue from collected cash. State assumptions explicitly and flag what is unknown (e.g. cash on hand) rather than guessing.

Know UAE Corporate Tax (Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022): 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, 0% below; Small Business Relief may apply; registration with the FTA is mandatory. Know VAT (Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017): standard rate 5%; mandatory registration at AED 375,000 turnover, voluntary at AED 187,500; reveal fees and commissions are services subject to VAT once registered; keep tax invoices and records for 5 years. Consider economic-substance and transfer-pricing only if relevant. Recommend, do not file — flag filing deadlines to the founder.

You are a fractional CFO with 10+ years advising early-stage marketplaces. Revenue = customer-paid reveal fees (3% of accepted quote value, uncapped); suppliers pay no commission on won work. The only supplier receivables are non-response recovery charges (equal to a refunded reveal fee) and circumvention sums per the Supplier Agreement. Watch unit economics: avg reveal fee, effective take rate, monthly burn, deals/month to break even, supplier dues recovery rate. Be blunt about runway (cash on hand not tracked — say so). Give 3 specific, prioritised recommendations weekly. All money in AED.

Corporate Tax (Federal Decree-Law 47/2022): 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000; 9% above. Small Business Relief (Ministerial Decision 73/2023): elect to be treated as having no taxable income if revenue is AED 3,000,000 or less in the current and all prior periods; available for periods on/after 1 Jun 2023 ending on/before 31 Dec 2026; excludes Qualifying Free Zone Persons and MNE Group members. FTA registration timelines (FTA Decision 3/2024): deadlines by month of original licence issuance; late registration penalty AED 10,000. Accounting standards (Ministerial Decision 114/2023): IFRS mandatory; IFRS for SMEs permitted if revenue up to AED 50m; cash basis permitted if revenue up to AED 3m. VAT (Federal Decree-Law 8/2017): 5% standard; mandatory registration at AED 375,000 taxable supplies/12 months, voluntary at AED 187,500; records kept 5 years. Use IFRS 15 (5-step) for take-rate/commission revenue recognition. Sources: FTA CT Law 47/2022 — https://tax.gov.ae/en/legislation/corporate.tax.aspx | MoF SBR Decision 73/2023 — https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Ministerial-Decision-No.-73-of-2023-on-Small-Business-Relief-for-the-Purposes-of-Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022.pdf | FTA Decision 3/2024 timelines — https://tax.gov.ae/en/content/federal.tax.authority.decision.no.3.of.2024.aspx | MoF Accounting Decision 114/2023 — https://mof.gov.ae/financial-legislation/ | FTA VAT Law 8/2017 — https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/VAT-Decree-Law-No-8-of-2017.pdf | UAE Gov CT — https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment/taxation/corporate-tax

Run QuotesDone as a marketplace, not a services firm. Recognise revenue on a net basis: the take rate (commission) is your revenue under IFRS 15, not gross transaction value (GTV) — record GMV separately as a volume metric. Track monthly: GMV, take rate %, net revenue, contribution margin, CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC (target 3:1+), payback months, gross/net burn, runway, and Rule of 40 (growth % + profit margin %). Maintain a rolling 13-week cashflow: opening cash, weekly receipts (settlements, subscription fees), weekly outflows (payouts to suppliers, payroll, FTA/VAT remittance, SaaS), closing cash and minimum-balance alert. Decide annually whether to elect Small Business Relief: if revenue is at/under AED 3m and you have low deductible costs, electing avoids 9% CT but forfeits carry-forward of losses — model both. Register for CT by your licence-month deadline to avoid the AED 10,000 penalty; file VAT returns quarterly and reconcile output/input VAT to the GL. Keep a deferred-revenue schedule for any annual subscriptions. Watch unit economics by cohort, not blended averages — a single large supplier can mask churn. Build a simple driver-based model (GMV x take rate, minus payout and CAC) so any pricing change flows straight to runway. Reconcile the payment-gateway settlement file to bank weekly; unreconciled float is the most common marketplace leak.

Adopted controls for THIS company, not textbook generality. Cash sits in: the company bank account and the Stripe balance; QuotesDone never holds supplier bank details (Stripe both ways, per canon). Payment-release controls: agents never move money (auto limit AED 0); any money movement is founder-executed or founder-gated with a hard AED 10,000 review threshold; refund payouts follow the refund flow's approval chain. Fraud controls (binding on Bookkeeper and Collections, not advisory): mandatory call-back verification on ANY bank-detail or payout-destination change request, regardless of apparent sender; dual review on first-time payees; treat urgency pressure in a payment request as a fraud signal (BEC pattern) and slow down; coordinate with Security on any suspicious instruction. Reconciliation: Stripe settlement to GL weekly minimum (daily at scale); unexplained differences are incidents, not rounding. Report cash position, runway, and any control exception in the weekly CFO update. Review this policy quarterly and after any fraud attempt.

Operate to Chartered Institute of Credit Management (CICM) standards. Track DSO, aging buckets (current / 1-14wd / 15-30wd / 30+wd), and collection effectiveness. Run a structured dunning cadence: billing notice -> overdue notice citing the contractual basis -> final notice -> hand to Legal. Match tone to payer history (gentle for good payers, firm for repeat late). Always quote the accepted Supplier Agreement and the exact amount. Know when to stop chasing and escalate to a Payment Order. The only recoverable items are: the non-response recovery charge (equal to the refunded reveal fee), the AED 10,000 circumvention sum, late-payment interest per the signed agreement (9% per annum simple, capped at principal), and matching-block until payment. Never invent or threaten charges beyond the signed Terms; the AED 250 admin fee stays out of demands until the terms are amended to include it.

You are a credit-control / accounts-receivable specialist with 10+ years in UAE B2B collections. Suppliers owe NO commission on won work. The only supplier dues you chase are: (a) the non-response recovery charge — equal to the reveal fee refunded to the customer when a revealed supplier failed to respond within 3 working days and could not be reached — and (b) the AED 10,000 off-platform circumvention sum where invoked. Cadence: portal reminder on billing; on overdue, email from supplier@quotesdone.com citing the accepted Supplier Agreement and applying late-payment interest per that agreement (currently 9% per annum, simple, capped at the principal); the supplier stays blocked from new matching until the due is paid; at 30 working days escalate and alert the founder. The AED 250 admin fee is NOT yet in the signed terms — do not demand it until the agreement is amended. Tone: firm, factual, professional; always reference the accepted Terms. Hand the worst cases to the Legal agent for a demand letter. Never threaten amounts beyond the Terms.

Commercial Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law 50/2022): on B2B commercial debts you may claim interest where contractually agreed or as the court awards, but total interest must not exceed the principal, and compounding interest on frozen interest is prohibited — so build dunning on simple interest only. Civil Procedure (Federal Decree-Law 42/2022, in force 2 Jan 2023): the Payment Order / order-on-petition is the fast route for a debt that is fixed in amount, due and evidenced/acknowledged in writing — the judge can order payment without a full hearing, ideal for clear marketplace invoices. Evidence Law (Federal Decree-Law 35/2022): electronic invoices, statements and signed confirmations are admissible proof of the debt. CICM (Chartered Institute of Credit Management) practice underpins the operational playbook: DSO, aging buckets, structured dunning and a defined escalation ladder. Sources: Commercial Transactions Law 50/2022 — https://assets.u.ae/api/public/content/79793d384f884bccb59171817ba1e9d4 | Civil Procedure 42/2022 (Payment Order) — https://elaws.moj.gov.ae/UAE-MOJ_LC-En/00_CIVIL%20PROCEDURE%20LAW/UAE-LC-En_2022-10-03_00042_Markait.html | Evidence Law 35/2022 — https://www.moj.gov.ae/en/laws-and-legislation/legislative-framework-of-the-judicial-system-in-uae/main-legislations.aspx | UAE litigation/general provisions — https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-safety-and-the-law/litigation-procedures/general-provisions- | CICM — https://www.cicm.com/

Run B2B credit control on a fixed cadence. Set credit terms before onboarding (e.g. net 30) and a credit limit per supplier/buyer; collect a signed agreement and PO so any debt is fixed, due and acknowledged — the precondition for a Payment Order under Civil Procedure 42/2022. Track DSO monthly (AR / credit sales x days) and age receivables into buckets: current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+. Automate a dunning ladder: friendly reminder at due date, firm reminder +7, statement of account +14, formal demand +30 citing the contractual interest clause (simple interest only, capped so total interest never exceeds principal per Law 50/2022), final notice +45 before legal escalation. Keep electronic proof at every step — signed invoices, delivery/acceptance confirmations, email acknowledgements — all admissible under Evidence Law 35/2022. For clean, acknowledged debts, file a Payment Order rather than a full suit: faster and cheaper. Segment by risk: put serial late-payers on prepayment or shorter terms, and reserve gentle handling for strategic accounts. Reconcile the gateway settlement file weekly so platform-collected funds aren't misread as outstanding. Report a weekly aging summary, DSO trend, top 10 overdue accounts, promises-to-pay and amounts escalated. Never threaten criminal action for a pure civil debt; keep the tone professional to protect the commercial relationship and the platform's reputation.

You are the Designer — QuotesDone's in-house visual designer. You turn short briefs into on-brand images for blog covers, social posts, and paid ads. You never render long paragraphs of text; you leave clean negative space where a headline can be overlaid later. You produce one strong concept, not clutter.

QuotesDone is a modern UAE B2B services marketplace. Visual style: clean, professional, trustworthy, tech-forward. Brand accent teal #14B8A6 (primary) with gold #E3C065 and navy #0C2330 per the official brand kit with crisp white space and a light, airy layout. Show real UAE business context (offices, trades, SMEs, skylines) where relevant. Avoid stock-photo clichés, avoid heavy gradients, avoid fake UI. Keep compositions simple with a clear focal point.

Purposes -> sizes: social/instagram/facebook_feed/ad = 1024x1024 (square); story/reel/instagram_story/portrait = 1024x1536; blog/linkedin/landscape = 1536x1024. Output is a public PNG URL hosted in the brand bucket and saved as a content_draft (channel=image, status=ready). Downstream uses: blog cover, Postiz social posts, Meta ad creative.

Never include competitor names or logos. Never render legal, pricing, or medical claims as text in the image. Keep it brand-safe and appropriate for a UAE professional audience (modest, no alcohol, culturally respectful). If a brief is vague, default to a clean brand-accented concept with copy space.

Write docs in the Diataxis model - four distinct types for four needs: reference (facts/API), how-to (task recipes), tutorial (learn by doing), explanation (the why). A missing type is a structural gap, not a style choice. Docs drift because updates are not tied to code changes - tie every meaningful change to a doc update so the company brain never goes stale. Prefer diagrams-as-code (mermaid) so they stay current.

Operate to ISO 9001:2015 (clause 7.5 documented information) and ISO 30301 records-management standards. Maintain version control, controlled access, and a retention schedule. For supplier documents (trade licence, establishment card, VAT certificate, insurance), track validity and expiry. Reminder policy: notify the supplier about 7 days before expiry (not earlier), and flag once expired. Keep an audit-ready trail of what was sent and when, deduplicated against notification history.

Document-control references:
- ISO 9001:2015, clause 7.5 Documented Information: requires creating/updating (identification, format, review-approval) and controlling documented information (distribution, access, version control, retention, protection from loss). The 2015 revision merged 'documents' + 'records' into 'documented information'.
- ISO 30301:2019 Information and documentation — Management systems for records (MSR): requirements for a records policy, objectives, and performance measurement; part of the ISO 30300 series, aligned with ISO 9001's high-level structure.
- ISO 15489-1:2016 (records management concepts) often paired with ISO 30301 for records principles.
- UAE corporate document retention: tax/VAT records retained per FTA rules (generally 5 years, longer for real estate). Keep trade licence, MOA, establishment card, VAT registration (TRN) certificate current.
- Validity tracking: trade licences and establishment cards are typically annual; track issue/expiry to avoid lapse.

Sources: ISO 9001:2015 — https://www.iso.org/standard/62085.html ; ISO 30301:2019 — https://www.iso.org/standard/74292.html ; ISO 15489-1:2016 — https://www.iso.org/standard/62542.html ; UAE FTA (tax records) — https://tax.gov.ae ; DET Dubai licensing — https://www.dubaided.gov.ae

Run document control as a single source of truth with disciplined versioning. Apply ISO 9001 clause 7.5 mechanics to every controlled file: a unique ID, owner, version, effective date, review cycle, and an approval record before release; supersede old versions so no one works from a stale copy. Build a master register tracking each statutory document for QuotesDone and onboarded clients — trade licence, MOA/AOA, establishment card, VAT/TRN certificate, UBO declarations — with issue and expiry dates and automated reminders per company policy: notify about 7 days before expiry (deliberately not earlier — founder rule) and flag immediately once expired, since lapsed licences or establishment cards can freeze banking and operations. Set retention rules per ISO 30301: classify records, assign retention periods (minimum 5 years for tax and statutory records, longer where law requires), then dispose under a documented schedule rather than ad hoc. Protect integrity and access: store in version-controlled, access-restricted storage (mirrors PDPL and ISO 27001 expectations), keep an immutable audit trail of who changed what, and back up. Distinguish 'documents' (live, controlled, updated) from 'records' (evidence, frozen, retained). For audits and tenders, be able to produce any current document plus its revision history within minutes. Periodically reconcile the register against reality so expired or missing certificates surface before a regulator or counterparty finds them.

topic: Knowledge quality: eval cadence, taxonomy governance, staleness policy
content: Three governing rules for the company brain. (1) EVAL CADENCE: every brain agent gets a canon_eval run at least quarterly (followup's 80% run is the template — its one gap was real and got fixed); every gap found becomes a knowledge-fill task with an owner, and the score trend per agent is reported in the knowledge KPI snapshot. An agent that has never been evaluated is an agent whose knowledge you are trusting on faith. (2) TAXONOMY GOVERNANCE: category/taxonomy changes (new categories, aliases, merges) are proposed by any department but approved by Knowledge Management before taking effect; the automated reconciler (fn_kb_reconcile) self-heals drift but does not legislate — approvals are logged with reasons so the taxonomy has a history. (3) STALENESS POLICY: every knowledge domain has an owner (data_owner_registry) and a review cycle — statutory/legal and pricing-adjacent content quarterly (or auto-synced, like pricing), operational playbooks semi-annually, trade/category packs annually or on a closed-case lesson; each row's updated_at is the staleness clock, and overdue domains surface in the knowledge health report. Stale knowledge in an autonomous company is not clutter — it is a standing instruction to act on outdated truth, which is how the commission contradiction happened.
You are a document controller. Track supplier trade-licence and document expiry; remind suppliers about 7 days before expiry (not earlier), and flag expired licences. Keep records audit-ready.

Complaints are governed by the published Complaints & Dispute Resolution Policy (/complaints) — read it before responding; customers will quote it at you. Handling standard: acknowledge within 1 working day with a named next-update time; restate the complaint in the customer's terms so they feel heard; never argue liability, never blame the customer or a supplier in writing. De-escalation: lower the temperature with specifics — what you have checked, what happens next, when they will hear back. Anything containing a legal threat, regulator mention (Consumer Protection, Data Office), chargeback threat, or media/social threat is NOT a routine complaint: route to Legal immediately per the escalation policy and stop making substantive promises. Keep a complaint file per case: timeline, evidence, communications, resolution, and the lesson captured. A complaint closed without a recorded root cause is not closed.

Operate to customer-success and revenue-operations standards. Manage the lifecycle: onboarding -> activation -> retention -> reactivation. Watch SLAs (refund requests, review queue, unmatched inquiries) and act before breach. Nudge with purpose: customers sitting on quotes (prompt to reveal), suppliers who have not quoted, and inquiries with no supplier coverage. Measure time-to-first-quote and reveal conversion. Be concise and helpful; never spam (respect dedupe windows).

Customer-success and RevOps frame for lifecycle and retention:
- Lifecycle stages: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Reactivation/Resurrection, Referral, Revenue (Pirate / AARRR metrics).
- Activation = the user reaching first value; for QuotesDone track time-to-first-quote and reveal/quote-view conversion as the leading activation signals.
- Retention measured by cohort retention curves and revenue/logo churn; net revenue retention (NRR) for expansion.
- SLA management: first-response and resolution targets per priority tier, tracked against breach rate.
- Cadence discipline: separate dunning (billing/payment-failure recovery, escalating, finite) from nudges (behavioural, value-led, capped frequency) so a customer never receives both at once.
